messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: DNS alert — elevated error rate observed for eu edge namespace at 2026-03-14T09:00:00Z. Monitoring reports NXDOMAIN/SERVFAIL spikes
sara: noticing user-facing 502/504s from EU customers starting ~09:00 UTC. Error graphs show DNS timeouts and inconsistent answers for some api/embeddings hostnames
mike: synthetic probes confirm instability. From eu probe: ~5% of requests to api.eu.redwood.test time out with `connection timed out` or `SERVFAIL`
anya: looking at resolver logs — there are mismatched answers coming back from Cloudflare vs Route53 for geo-enabled records
lee-oncall: taking this incident. assign to me; what's the immediate blast radius? which hostnames?
sara: primary affected: api.eu.redwood.test, embeddings.eu.redwood.test, model-meta.eu.redwood.test. Impact concentrated in eu-west-1 and some APAC traffic routed to EU geonodes. Error rate peaking ~4-6% on sensitive endpoints
mike: quick `dig` snapshot from probes:
```
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.eu.redwood.test
# sometimes returns 10.10.5.12
# sometimes returns NXDOMAIN
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.eu.redwood.test
# returns 10.10.6.20
```
mike: seems Cloudflare edge resolvers and Route53 authoritative answers disagree intermittently
anya: CF origin health checks are noisy for a subset of origin IPs; CF appears to mark some origins down, which may change DNS answers on their layer
lee-oncall: immediate mitigations? propose: 1) reduce TTL to short window, 2) purge CF DNS/cache for affected names, 3) pin geo answers to Route53 as temporary authoritative fallback, 4) escalate CF support
sara: lowering TTLs to 30s on Route53 on affected records now. will also purge CF cache for the hostnames (non-disruptive)
mike: runbook snippet for TTL update (Route53 UPSERT example):
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZZZ --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.eu.redwood.test","Type":"A","TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"10.10.6.20"}]}}]}'
```
anya: opened cloudflare ticket (CF-INC-98765). purged `api.eu.redwood.test` and related records. CF auto-reply: we see origin health propagation delays in region, investigating
cloudflare-support: (auto) we've received your ticket, logs indicate a control-plane to edge propagation lag affecting origin-health updates in EU. investigating, ETA ~15-30m
lee-oncall: perform a canary to validate Route53-only answers before wide roll. pick a non-prod subdomain and pin to Route53 to validate behavior
sara: created canary `canary.api.eu.redwood.test` and UPSERTed to Route53 at 09:08 UTC
mike: canary probe results: stable, no NXDOMAINs for 12 minutes after pinning
anya: pushing staged change: align Route53 canonical answers across geo records and temporarily disable CF geo overrides for priority hostnames
ops-bot: Mitigation runbook (short):
1) Set Route53 TTLs to 30s for affected records
2) Purge Cloudflare DNS cache and HTTP cache for impacted hostnames
3) Temporarily set Route53 as single geo-authority (remove CF geo-overrides or set CF to pass-through)
4) Monitor synthetic probes and error rate for 15m moving window
5) If stable, ramp TTLs 30 -> 60 -> 300s over 1h
6) If errors persist >5% after 20m, execute traffic shift to fallback region
sara: implemented steps 1 & 2 at 09:12 UTC, started monitoring dashboards
anya: CF ticket updated with zone list and sample traces: api.eu.redwood.test, embeddings.eu.redwood.test, model-meta.eu.redwood.test
cloudflare-support: update: identified delayed propagation of origin health-state in regional control plane affecting edge resolvers; fix being applied to control plane now
mike: because CF is in the middle of control-plane fix, I'm going to flip geo authority to Route53-only for the affected prefix to eliminate split-brain answers
lee-oncall: proceed. if stabilization takes >10m, prep a status page message and customer comms
sara: drafted status page note and will publish if we hit 10m sustained customer impact
anya: Route53-only change applied at 09:20 UTC. within 5 minutes, error rate dropped from ~4% to ~0.8%
mike: sample health probe after change (09:25 UTC): HTTP 200 responses for /health endpoints consistently
lee-oncall: good progress. keep monitoring for 30m and do not revert TTLs until CF confirms full convergence
cloudflare-support: rollback/update: control plane fix deployed at 09:36 UTC; edge convergence estimated 10-15m due to caching TTLs
sara: starting TTL ramp at 09:48 UTC: increased TTL from 30s to 60s for stable zones
anya: recommend keeping health-check frequency elevated and tracing errors to verify no client-side caching anomalies for 1h
mike: post-incident notes: probable root cause is interplay between CF origin-health flapping and our geo-DNS updates causing temporary inconsistent authoritative answers (split-brain). Add preflight checks before geo rollouts and an automated fallback for mixed-authority detection
lee-oncall: assigning postmortem owners: sara (incident lead), mike (network lead), anya (cloud provider liaison). I'll write the initial incident timeline and severity assessment
sara: paging closed at 10:15 UTC; incident moved to monitoring and postmortem follow-up
ops-bot: archived thread and created PM stub PM-2026-03-14-02
mike: follow-ups added to PM: integration test for mixed-authority DNS answers, rollback hooks in geodns pipeline, clearer CF escalation playbook
anya: I'll request a deeper RCA from CF TAC and ask about possible credits for the disruption
sara: thanks all for quick coordination. :thumbsup:
